A9-01.kft: Experiment (interruption vs no-interruption): the context of interruptions did not make a difference, but participants completed interrupted tasks in LESS time with no difference in quality; the data SUGGEST people compensate for interruptions by working faster, at the price of experiencing more stress, higher frustration, time pressure, and effort (hedge per source); individual differences exist: openness to experience and need for personal structure predict disruption costs - the same interruption stream feels different to different people.
A9-01.ess: not_quantifiable (directional; charted from full text - compensation-by-speed, no quality difference, increased stress/frustration/time pressure/effort; specific statistics in the paper; no magnitude implied)
A9-01.lim: Lab setting with artificial tasks and small N; single-session; interruption medium/context manipulation is message-style (null context effect bounded to that manipulation); compensation mechanism inferred from speed data, not directly measured; quality measures task-specific and may be insensitive to compensation costs; experiential outcomes (stress/effort/time pressure) are self-reported - they are the capture channel itself, not weaker evidence; 2008-era interruption paradigm differs from modern notification regimes.
A9-01.di: Interruptions carry hidden costs (stress, effort, time pressure) even when output is preserved - the pilot must measure these (subjective workload/stress/effort as mandatory DVs), not just completion time and quality, or it replicates the 'no difference' illusion; interruption costs are personally variable (personality moderators) - design must not assume a uniform felt cost; support resumption and reduce interruption-driven compensation (queueing/batching, resumption cues).
A9-01.dimpl: Workday Interruption Protocol: code interruption queueing/batching and resumption cues as conditions; measure compensation-by-speed explicitly (speed-up is the mechanism, not the benefit); require a baseline/no-interruption contrast (SCED logic); direction + bounded band only, no point estimates from the paper.
A9-01.cimpl: The interruption regime is a candidate technics of attention (Tier-P, lab-bounded): it orders the person's attention - what may interrupt, when, and at what felt cost; the felt cost is irreducibly the person's own, varying with the person (openness, need for personal structure).

A9-02.kft: Fieldwork observation of information workers (analysts, developers, managers) documents that workers EXPERIENCE constant discontinuity of activity - the paper's own title: 'constant, constant, multi-tasking craziness'. Calibrated: ~3 minutes per task and ~2+ minutes per tool before switching; people work in ~10 'working spheres' (larger, thematically connected units of work - the person's own emic organizational structure), ~12 minutes per sphere before switching. IT design should support people's continual switching between working spheres.
A9-02.ess: not_quantifiable (descriptive observational metrics - minutes per task/tool/sphere - are not effect sizes; 2004-era)
A9-02.lim: Single organization observed; descriptive means only, no inferential statistics computed; observation-granularity artifacts; 2004-era knowledge-work tooling (switching rates are era- and tooling-bound, NOT normative targets); working spheres is the researchers' documented interpretation of an emic construct (not directly user-reported in this study).
A9-02.di: Design for working spheres (thematic units), not isolated tasks: the interruption queue and resumption logic should be sphere-aware (sphere resumption, cross-sphere continuity); avoid task-centric single-window assumptions; do NOT set interruption thresholds from the 2004 figures - measure the pilot's own discontinuity baseline; fragmentation (switching rate, sphere count) is a legitimate pilot outcome metric.
A9-02.dimpl: Workday Interruption Protocol: the experienced discontinuity (the felt 'craziness') is the phenomenon to address, not merely the measured intervals - the tool must respect the user's own sphere structure and the felt toll of constant switching.
A9-02.cimpl: Working spheres are a documented ordering of the person's work-activity (emic by researchers' interpretation, not direct self-report); the felt toll of constant switching is the lived face of discontinuity; the tool should mirror the user's sphere structure - as a REVISABLE locality (the user can restructure it, S10), not a frozen identity (localism).
A9-02.cs: correlational (descriptive-observational: field observation, no manipulation, no inferential statistics)

A9-04.kft: Two lab experiments: people need to stop thinking about one task in order to fully transition attention and perform well on another; it is difficult to disengage attention from an unfinished task and subsequent task performance suffers; finishing the task before switching is NOT enough - time pressure while finishing is needed to disengage from the first task and contributes to higher performance on the next task.
A9-04.ess: not_quantifiable (abstract-level; lab performance measures; specific statistics in full text, which is institutional)
A9-04.lim: Abstract-level charting (full text ScienceDirect paywalled; abstract RePEc-verified); task types, samples, and effect magnitudes unknown at abstract level; the mechanism behind the time-pressure finding (why pressure enables disengagement) is not explained in the abstract; the 'finishing is not enough' result may interact with task difficulty - unverifiable at abstract level.
A9-04.di: Task closure affordances alone will not eliminate residue costs ('finish before switching' is NOT enough): closure affordances exist FOR THE FELT WEIGHT of the unfinished work (residue as felt remainder, the haunting no performance metric captures), not only for the performance cost; provide resumption support beyond closure (resumption cues, disengagement rituals); time-pressure-as-disengagement levers must be tested ONLY with the A9-01 stress/effort cost measurements - never as a standalone feature; measure next-task performance in the immediate post-switch window (the residue window).
A9-04.dimpl: Arousal/Flow/Task-Switching Layer: attention residue is a felt remainder that persists after task completion - design closure and disengagement affordances for the felt weight of unfinished work; treat time-pressure levers with stress caveats (cf. A9-01); residue and time-pressure effects are lab-task results, not validated design levers.
A9-04.cimpl: Attention residue is measured as a next-task performance decrement; the charting reads it as a phenomenological remainder (Tier-P, interpretive - the source does not measure the felt experience): the unfinished task persists into the next; the tool's switch-design shapes the continuity of the person's attention and the felt weight of the unfinished.

A9-05.kft: The review targets information overload AS EXPERIENCED - perceived overload exacerbated by the digitalization of work, the felt excess that no message count or intervention menu captures. Method: PRISMA systematic review; 87 studies, field reports, and conceptual papers on prevention/intervention measures. Results: many interventions at the behavioral prevention level; structural-prevention proposals also numerous (work design at the ICT level and at the teamwork/organizational-regulation level); the strength of evidence across studies is MIXED.
A9-05.ess: not_quantifiable (no pooling; 'the strength of the evidence... is mixed' is itself the headline finding)
A9-05.lim: Mixed/heterogeneous evidence base; many included items are conceptual papers or field reports, not controlled studies; structural-level proposals largely untested; no risk-of-bias grading reported in the abstract; review scope limited to prevention/intervention literature (no evidence on overload prevalence or consequences); possible language/geography skew (German-affiliated review team) - flagged, not asserted.
A9-05.di: Multi-level intervention menu (behavioral + structural: ICT design, teamwork/organizational regulation); treat every reviewed intervention as a candidate hypothesis, not a proven measure; structural proposals must not be imported as validated; felt/perceived overload must be MEASURED, not inferred from message counts - the pilot's DV should include perceived overload; document the evidence level (behavioral vs structural) of each intervention the pilot touches.
A9-05.dimpl: Workday Interruption Protocol: information overload is a milieu condition with a felt face - the tool must reduce informational noise as part of cultivating the person's attentional cosmos, with structural (not just behavioral) responsibility; mixed evidence means the pilot measures its own outcomes.
A9-05.cimpl: Information overload is a milieu condition: the felt excess is the phenomenon (the source's own 'as experienced' framing); the intervention taxonomy charts the response surface - it does not calibrate the felt condition; the tool must address perceived overload before optimizing message flows; structural responsibility for the informational environment is a proposal-level claim (mixed evidence; Tier-P).
A9-05.cs: correlational (mixed-evidence systematic review; no causal claim licensed about any intervention)

A9-06.kft: One-day diary study (492 German office workers): interruption frequency relates to subjective workload THROUGH the individual's perception of the interruptions (statistical mediation - cross-sectional, causal order NOT established); the complexity of the primary work task moderates the effect - more complex primary tasks SEEM to strengthen the positive relationship between interruption frequency and subjective workload (hedge per source).
A9-06.ess: not_quantifiable (abstract-level; direction + significance only; no coefficients reported in the abstract; an open CC-BY PDF exists on the RWTH record but is bot-challenged to agents - abstract-level charting is a documented decision, not a paywall)
A9-06.lim: Common-method variance (frequency, perception, workload all self-reported same day); end-of-day recall bias; single day may not represent typical workload; German office-worker sample; complexity operationalization unknown at abstract level; mediation is statistical, not causal - routinely over-read as causal, must not be charted as a mechanism; RWTH record's 'Review Article' tag is a repository quirk (the study is empirical).
A9-06.di: Interruption perception/appraisal is the operative locus - interventions could target appraisal rather than (only) reducing interruption frequency; complexity moderation means low-complexity phases are less affected, so blanket interruption bans are overkill; use objective interruption logs alongside self-report to avoid the common-method bias the source itself suffers from; context-sensitive policy, not blanket rules.
A9-06.dimpl: Workday Interruption Protocol: protect complex-task phases from interruption, with complexity PERSON-DESIGNATED or person-confirmed (never a tool-side classifier - S1/S10 guard, Ethics Auditor); treat interruption perception/appraisal as a measured mediator AND as an intervention target in the legibility/support sense (making interruptions understandable, resumable, chosen - the tool responds to the person's appraisal; explicitly NOT felt-cost down-regulation to preserve output - the batch's moral-hollowing failure mode, Ethics Auditor); subjective workload as a key outcome metric; use objective interruption logs alongside self-report; context-sensitive policy, not blanket rules; direction-only import (no coefficients at abstract level).
A9-06.cimpl: The perceived interruption is the locus of cost: appraisal (what the interruption felt like, why it felt costly) mediates the frequency->workload relation (Tier-P - statistical mediation, cross-sectional, causal order not established; no magnitude equality licensed); the tool's interruption grammar participates in shaping the person's experienced ordering of work.
A9-06.cs: correlational (cross-sectional one-day diary; mediation is statistical, causal order not established)

CORE-09.kft: Self-regulation operates through cybernetic feedback control: behavior is regulated by comparing the current state against reference standards, and the FELT discrepancy - the inner experience of not being where one should be - motivates corrective action (negative feedback loops); control operates across a hierarchy of levels (motor programs to behavioral systems to self); self-awareness engages the self-referential level, intensifying discrepancy monitoring; where discrepancy reduction is impeded, withdrawal/disengagement from the behavioral stream may follow; the framework's integrative potential for personality, social, clinical, and health psychology is SUGGESTED, not demonstrated.
CORE-09.ess: not_quantifiable (theoretical framework article; no pooled ES)
CORE-09.lim: Conceptual synthesis; cybernetic metaphor carries information-processing assumptions; predictions require specifying reference values and loop parameters; not empirically tested as a whole in this article; the felt discrepancy-experience is the referent the loop models - the mechanism must not be mistaken for the phenomenon; later Carver & Scheier revisions add approach/positive-feedback dynamics beyond pure discrepancy reduction.
CORE-09.di: Standards-based self-monitoring is the grammar of self-regulation: support reference-setting (goal standards), discrepancy feedback, and resumption of corrective action; design for the hierarchy (task-level loops within self-level standards); the felt experience of self-monitoring precedes the loop mechanics - capture it first.
CORE-09.dimpl: Arousal/Flow/Task-Switching Layer: self-regulation as governed return - the feedback loop is the person's own grammar of return to their affirmed order; the tool should support the person's standards, not substitute its own.
CORE-09.cimpl: Self-regulation as governed return: the loop models the felt discrepancy-experience - the tool must keep the person's own standards as the reference (S1 guard) and support the felt return, not merely the correction; the cybernetic frame itself must not be operationalized as a steerable-system design - HUI-2024 (with Heidegger) identifies cybernetics with the completion of the manipulation paradigm (steuerbare Einrichtung), so a loop-based tool that treats the person as the plant is precisely the capture the cosmotechnic reading must refuse (medium Cosmo Rel.).

CORE-10.kft: Originator-authored 35-year review of goal-setting research: specific and difficult goals lead to higher performance than easy or vague ('do your best') goals, given goal commitment, feedback, and task-appropriate strategy; goals operate through four mechanisms (direction of attention, effort, persistence, strategy development); moderators include goal commitment (a felt state), feedback, and task complexity; goals mediate the effects of incentives; the relation of goals and SATISFACTION (the felt/affective consequence of goal attainment) is among the reviewed contents; external validity and practical significance are emphasized.
CORE-10.ess: not_quantifiable from charted source (narrative review; no pooled ES in this article; do NOT import external meta-analytic values - batch convention)
CORE-10.lim: Originator-authored narrative review (Locke & Latham reviewing their own theory) - advocacy-adjacent, NOT independent confirmation; no search protocol, no pooling; goal effects strongest for simple tasks (complex/creative tasks invert: learning goals outperform performance goals); assumes conscious, rational goal pursuit; publication-bias/file-drawer not addressed; negative goal effects flagged only via an external row (CORE-11), not the source.
CORE-10.di: Goal effects are conditional on commitment and feedback - without them, difficult goals can backfire; if goals narrow attention excessively in complex or creative work, performance and quality suffer (goal-performance relation inverts); externally imposed goals interact with incentives (cf. CORE-05/CORE-06 crowding: imposed goals may crowd internal commitment).
CORE-10.dimpl: Monstare Protocol vNext: goal specificity and difficulty as levers, gated on commitment, feedback, and task complexity; use learning goals for complex tasks; watch the interaction with incentives (crowding risk per CORE-05/06); avoid goal imposition - the goal's telos stays the person's own (S1 guard) and the goal architecture itself is user-revisable/removable (S10, Ethics Auditor); the felt/affective side of goal pursuit (satisfaction, commitment) is part of the design space, not an afterthought.
CORE-10.cimpl: Goal-setting is a technics of directed attention (source-sanctioned mechanism: direction of attention, effort, persistence); the cosmotechnic content is the telos guard - the goal's telos must remain the person's own; under the criterion that a technics must serve the person's affirmed order of value (A1-01), goal-assignment by the tool converts the person's directedness into the tool's output function, an output instrument (Tier-P - a verdict derived from the criterion, NOT a source claim; the source's paradigm imposes goals and shows performance gains).
CORE-10.cs: causal (experimental program, per originator review - goal difficulty manipulated in cited lab/field experiments; not independent confirmation)

CORE-15.kft: Experiment (120 participants, disgusting film; process model as framing): both reappraisal (antecedent-focused) and suppression (response-focused) reduced emotion-expressive behavior; reappraisal decreased the EXPERIENCE of disgust; suppression INCREASED sympathetic activation; the two emotion regulatory processes have different adaptive consequences - the inner split under suppression (feeling the emotion while hiding it, the body paying) is the row's non-rational remainder.
CORE-15.ess: not_quantifiable (abstract-level; significant behavioral/experiential/physiological differences; specific statistics in full text, which is institutional)
CORE-15.lim: Abstract-level charting (PubMed record; APA full text institutional); single emotion (disgust) and single induction (film); short-term measurement; 'increased sympathetic activation' framed as a physiological COST is an interpretive inference (sympathetic arousal is a marker); 'reappraisal may fail under cognitive load' is an external inference, tagged as such, not a source claim; cultural moderation of suppression effects is an external boundary condition, not charted.
CORE-15.di: Suppression's increased sympathetic activation implies costs of response-focused regulation (interpretive, Tier-P); if reappraisal requires cognitive resources, it may be unavailable under load (inference, not source claim); strategy effectiveness depends on context and individual differences not covered here.
CORE-15.dimpl: Monstare Protocol vNext: emotion regulation is time-sensitive - support ANTECEDENT-focused regulation (reappraisal, situation modification) over response-focused (suppression); regulation timing (before vs after the emotion) is a design parameter; interruption flows must not force suppression (offer outlet/antecedent options - do not rely on reappraisal-only strategies in interruption-heavy conditions); the felt state is preserved before the timing parameter.
CORE-15.cimpl: Emotion regulation grammar: antecedent-focused regulation changes the felt state at its source (reappraisal reduced disgust experience); response-focused suppression splits felt experience from expressed behavior at a physiological price (increased sympathetic activation; 'cost' interpretive, Tier-P, with boundary conditions - reappraisal may fail under load, suppression has situational uses); the tool's temporal structure (when it interrupts, when it asks for emotion work) is morally consequential under the criterion that a technics must not force the person's affective life into a hidden split (S7: no morally hollow productivity).
